guarantees.promise: the HTTP gateway requires a credential on every non-public route
guarantees.needs: `gateway_auth_token`, or (`compliance`) a token table or `[oidc]`

guarantees.promise: a gateway bound beyond loopback requires a credential — `start()` refuses an open one unless explicitly waived; on a credentialed node `/health`, `/ready`, `/stats`, `/metrics`, `/bulk/{id}` and the A2A descriptor stay public, `/a2a` admits an anonymous caller, and a merged router's paths outside `/gateway/` are not gated
guarantees.needs: `gateway_auth_token`, or (`compliance`) a token table or `[oidc]`, on any non-loopback `http_addr`; `gateway_allow_unauthenticated` unset

guarantees.promise: scoped or named tokens close the gateway with a per-route scope floor
guarantees.needs: `compliance`; `gateway_scoped_tokens` / `gateway_named_tokens`

guarantees.promise: human operators authenticate to the gateway through the IdP, groups mapped to scopes
guarantees.needs: `compliance`; `[oidc]`

guarantees.promise: the gateway serves HTTPS, so bearers and JWTs do not cross the wire in cleartext
guarantees.needs: `tls`; `[gateway_tls]` (or TLS terminated by a proxy in front — not visible here)

guarantees.promise: a provider sees the gateway's client as the caller, attested by the gateway's identity
guarantees.needs: `tls`; `[tls]`; `gateway_caller_profile = secure` (the default)

guarantees.promise: gossip is mTLS: every peer presents a certificate signed by the fleet CA
guarantees.needs: `tls`; `[tls]`

guarantees.promise: an unsigned KV write frame, or one signed in the bare pre-2.33 form, is refused (a self-authenticating sealed identity record or CA-verified certificate record excepted), so a member cannot write as another by not signing — anti-entropy state replies excepted, and another member's identity stays writable under the writer's own signature unless `require_identity_proofs`
guarantees.needs: `tls`; `[tls]` (unconditional since post-360 row F2; `kv_require_signed_frames` is retired)

guarantees.promise: an identity entry this node cannot authenticate is rejected (issuer binding rests on it)
guarantees.needs: `tls`; `[tls]`; `require_identity_proofs` (default `true` since post-360 row S; `false` opts out)

guarantees.promise: the fleet CA's private key is not on this node — with it here, one compromised host can mint a certificate for every node in the fleet, so a removed member can mint itself a new identity and key revocation cannot recover a stolen identity (post-360 plan row T)
guarantees.needs: `tls`; `[tls] cert_pem` + `key_pem` (a node certificate issued off-node: `mycelium tls issue`); no `ca-key.pem` in this node's certificate directory

guarantees.promise: a revocation of this node's keys counts only when a newer certificate the fleet CA issued for it signs it, and no one without the CA key can issue one
guarantees.needs: `tls`; `[tls] cert_pem` + `key_pem` with a certificate naming the node by URI (`mycelium://<node>`, issued by `mycelium tls issue` since post-360 row Q); no `ca-key.pem` in this node's certificate directory

guarantees.promise: every gateway dispatch is authorised by policy before it runs — permit, deny or indeterminate
guarantees.needs: `gateway` + `tls`; `with_action_evaluator`

guarantees.promise: every authorisation decision is journalled, fsynced, before dispatch
guarantees.needs: `gateway` + `tls`; `with_action_evaluator` and `with_evidence_journal`

guarantees.promise: protected work (`mcp.invoke`, `skill.invoke`, …) is authorised where it runs, not only at a gateway
guarantees.needs: `gateway` + `tls`; `with_provider_enforcement` (with an evaluator; without one every protected call is refused)

guarantees.promise: `/a2a` is not anonymous skill dispatch
guarantees.needs: `a2a`; an evaluator that denies anonymous principals — a bearer does not gate this route

guarantees.promise: mandates are established and verified at this node (scoped authority, revocation)
guarantees.needs: `gateway` + `tls`; `with_execution_authority`

guarantees.promise: a restart does not restore revoked authority: installed epochs are journalled first
guarantees.needs: `gateway` + `tls`; `ExecutionAuthority::with_durable_epochs`

guarantees.promise: governance actions at the gateway are sealed into the tamper-evident chain
guarantees.needs: `compliance`; `[tls]` (records are sealed with the node identity)

guarantees.promise: sealed records are mirrored to an external sink (SIEM / WORM), original bytes kept
guarantees.needs: `compliance`; `[tls]`; `with_audit_sink`

guarantees.promise: the substrate's own outbound calls are restricted to a hostname allow-list (MCP bridge, LLM, probes, skillrunner, the wasm host, the wiki sink, the federation client, OIDC) — the first URL and every redirect hop, with the host read the way the client reads it
guarantees.needs: `egress.allow_hosts` non-empty (empty allows all); the federation client (the node's policy applied to clients it is handed, `FederationClient::with_egress` elsewhere) and OIDC discovery + JWKS since 2026-10-03 (a denied issuer refuses `start()`). Since 2.23.0: every redirect hop re-checked (≤ 5, never https → http), none followed by a client without the policy or carrying a credential header (`mycelium::egress_client`); the host parsed with the client's own WHATWG parser; an object store gated on the endpoint it dials, not its bucket. An `HttpLibrarySource` or `OllamaProbe` built outside an agent is gated only when built `with_egress`. **Not covered:** name resolution (an allowed name resolving to a denied address), a cloud identity's credential traffic, redirects inside `object_store`'s own client

guarantees.promise: a credential binding's value is attached at the egress gate only to a request for the host it names (on its port when it names one — a binding to `localhost` or an IP literal must; under its path prefix; over https or to loopback) — refused anywhere else, dropped on a redirect that leaves it, counted per binding, and never in a log, a `Debug`, an error or the evidence journal; a caller holds only its placeholder
guarantees.needs: `[[egress_credentials]]` (or `GOSSIP_EGRESS_CREDENTIALS`), values read once at `start()`; a caller that sends through the gate — `OpenAiBackend::with_credentials`, `[[serve]]`'s `credential`, `EgressCredentials::send` / `send_once`, an `[[activation]]` command through its stem's egress proxy (`[activation.confine.egress] credentials`). **Not covered:** a secret a component or command reads from its own environment or files (an `[[activation]]` command without `[activation.confine.egress]` has no path to the gate); a proxy the gate's client is configured with (`HTTP(S)_PROXY`) sees a plaintext or loopback request's header; a placeholder in a query string or body (not resolved); `api_key` / `api_key_env`, federation, object-store and git credentials, which keep their own paths

guarantees.promise: a restart recovers the KV and acceptor memory from disk
guarantees.needs: `[persistence]`

guarantees.promise: a WAL acknowledgement is a durability claim: the write is on disk before the ack
guarantees.needs: `[persistence]` with `sync_mode = "flush"` — the writer syncs only in `flush` (or on `append_sync`); `os` is buffered like `async`

guarantees.promise: a node does not start over persisted state it could not read — nothing is compacted over an unreadable snapshot or WAL
guarantees.needs: `[persistence]` with `on_unreadable = "refuse"` (the default)

guarantees.promise: the WAL and snapshot are encrypted at rest
guarantees.needs: `[persistence]`; `with_data_at_rest_cipher`, before `start()`

guarantees.promise: an exclusive outcome — a lock, a leader, a consistent write, a commitment award, a capability-authz policy, any proposal marked safety-sensitive — is decided only by an electorate group: one pinned by member identity, decided by every member it names and frozen after, whose acceptors answer only for their own electorate
guarantees.needs: `consensus_require_electorate = true`; the electorates declared (`/gateway/govern/electorate`), one marked `exclusive_default` for the cluster-scoped verbs. Its members are fixed at genesis — changing them is a migration that terminates: declare the successor naming the group, retire the group into it (closing it), complete the carry from a majority of it, after which the predecessor is never consulted (docs/design/consensus-electorate.md §8.3); a dead member lowers the group's fault tolerance until it is migrated, a lost majority stops it and cannot migrate. The fleet's default is declared once and moves only by the holder's retirement. The effect is still the caller's to fence at the resource

guarantees.promise: this node runs the enforced domain profile: TLS required and SWIM off, so membership at a federation boundary is never decided by unauthenticated UDP
guarantees.needs: `domain_profile = "enforced"` (`GOSSIP_DOMAIN_PROFILE`), with `swim_failure_detector = false` and `[tls]`, which `validate()` requires of it

guarantees.promise: every federation client dials its partner only over TLS terminated by a key the trust bundle pins (an `http://` endpoint is then refused, never called in the clear)
guarantees.needs: `FederationClient::with_tls_pins` on every client, from `TrustBundle::tls_pins_for`

guarantees.promise: the edge refuses a federated credential that does not bind the request body, so a payload rewritten between domains does not verify
guarantees.needs: `CallPolicy::require_body_binding = true` on the attached `FederationEdge` (the 2.12.0 rolling-upgrade window closed)

guarantees.promise: the edge carries at most a fixed number of calls from one partner at once, refusing the next rather than queuing it — per gateway, so N gateways admit N times the cap
guarantees.needs: `CallPolicy::max_in_flight_per_partner > 0` on the attached `FederationEdge`

guarantees.promise: on a gateway with federation clients, a credential is required, so a call made through `/gateway/federation/*` names an authenticated local caller rather than `anonymous` — the check `gw.not_open` makes, restated for the federation routes so the family says it; that the route mints under the resolved caller and never the node is by construction (`call_as`), not checked here
guarantees.needs: a gateway credential model (`gateway_auth_token`, or with `compliance` a token table or `[oidc]`) — the same predicate as `gw.not_open`; on an open gateway every call names `anonymous`

guarantees.promise: a catalogue is relied on only once it verifies under the partner's key, and the edge signs the catalogue it serves, so neither side acts on an export list a third party wrote
guarantees.needs: `FederationEdge::with_signing_key` on the edge; `FederationClient::with_partner_key` on every client

guarantees.promise: every partner endpoint a federation client dials is permitted by a non-empty egress allow-list the client is held to — by its exact host or by a `.suffix` entry, which admits every host under it, so a suffix entry covers more than the partner
guarantees.needs: `egress.allow_hosts` permitting each partner endpoint's host (the node's list reaches a client built without one), or `FederationClient::with_egress`; name the partner's host exactly to confine calls to it

guarantees.promise: a span built by `span_export` is not an evidence path: it carries a record's identity and outcome — its correlation, parent, rule and revision, outcome, a decision's typed reason, and its content hash as an opaque reference — never its inputs, target, effect, subject, resource, arguments, mandate or the audit chain's links; what was enforced is the record itself, read by that hash on the node that wrote it (`mycelium explain --closure` over its evidence journal, or over a decision trace where one is written) and verified there. The correlation is the caller's id, sent as given: one holding personal data puts it in every span of the run. **Outside this guarantee:** the skill runner's own spans (`skillrunner`, also under `otel`), which carry the caller
guarantees.needs: `otel`; a `span_export::SpanCollector` over the decision sink's tap and the evidence journal, sent through `span_export::otlp` — driven by the embedder

guarantees.promise: agent pods reach nothing but their gateway
guarantees.needs: the network: separate pods, an enforcing CNI, a NetworkPolicy

guarantees.promise: this node's wall clock is within the bound every expiry and freshness check assumes
guarantees.needs: deployment time-sync (NTP or equivalent)

guarantees.promise: the partner domain runs its side of the edge as this one does: pinned, body-bound, metered, signing its catalogue
guarantees.needs: the partner's own report — its `GET /gateway/guarantees` under `secure-multi-domain`, exchanged out of band

guarantees.promise: the two domains stay two meshes: no node of one is admitted to the other's gossip
guarantees.needs: separate CAs and networks per domain; the edge the only path between them

guarantees.promise: the partner's clock agrees with this node's within `CallPolicy::skew_tolerance`, which every credential window across the edge assumes
guarantees.needs: time-sync on both sides of the edge
